response.initial_request: The kitchen mixer tap is constantly dripping and wasting water. The water looks cloudy when I fill a glass. I suspect limescale may be involved and would like to know whether a new tap could be considered.

events.body: Reports a constantly dripping kitchen mixer tap and cloudy-looking water when filling a glass. Says limescale may be involved and asks whether a replacement tap could be considered. No urgency or access constraints are reported.
Requests approval to arrange plumbing work for the dripping tap and passes on the tenant's cloudy-water concern. Notes that limescale is the tenant's suspicion, not a confirmed cause.
Approves proceeding with the maintenance works. Says they are abroad until the following Wednesday and email is the best way to contact them.
Requests a quote or advice on whether a site visit is needed for the dripping mixer tap and cloudy-water report. No water sample or test result is available.
Follows up for a quote or confirmation that an inspection is needed. No response to the initial enquiry is recorded.
Explains that the contractor needs to attend to assess the plumbing work and asks for availability.
Offers 11, 13 and 14 August, all day, for an appointment.
Forwards the tenant's offered dates and asks the contractor to select a slot or propose an alternative.
Asks for further availability because the contractor has not selected a date.
Says they are home every day the following week except Monday.
Forwards the tenant's updated availability and requests a visit slot.

Says they are still waiting for contact about the leaking tap despite providing availability. Separately reports the top kitchen drawer is loose and its metal front brackets appear snapped; asks if it can be repaired when someone attends.

The contractor says other jobs prevent a firm date, but expects to review the schedule later that day and book the visit during the week. There is some confusion about the property address, which the manager repeats. No specific appointment is agreed.
Offers the following afternoon and asks whether the tenant will be available.

Says they will be at work from 11:00 the next day and authorizes the plumber to attend using the agency's spare key. The message does not address the drawer or provide new information about the cloudy water.
Confirms a visit for 10 September, with timing potentially varying because the contractor needs to collect keys from the office.
Says confirmation after 18:00 the previous evening is too late for scheduling and that they will try to accommodate the visit. Requests earlier confirmation for future bookings.
Apologizes for the late notice. Says the contractor may move the visit if unable to attend and can collect keys from the agency office. Requests an update on the date chosen.
An invoice describes a new mono kitchen sink tap supplied and installed. The invoice postcode differs from the property's recorded postcode, so it is queried.
Requests a corrected invoice showing the property's recorded postcode and asks the contractor to check whether any other invoice details need correction.

The contractor agrees to amend the postcode and resend the invoice. The conversation briefly turns to a separate boiler matter; the manager says they will check with the relevant engineer what work was done. No boiler work is documented as part of this tap job.
The corrected invoice shows the property's recorded postcode and describes a new mono kitchen sink tap supplied and installed. The invoice is awaiting operator review.

args.subject: Invoice NBL-025-INV-15 – amount missing – 18 Thistlewick Row, Fenmere, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body: Hello Ivo, thank you for the corrected invoice NBL-025-INV-15 for 18 Thistlewick Row, Fenmere, ZZ1 1ZZ. The postcode is now right, but the invoice shows no amount, so we can't pass it to the landlord. We also never received a quote for this job. Please resend the invoice with: (1) the total, with labour, the tap and VAT shown separately; (2) the date you attended and confirmation that the mono kitchen sink tap was supplied and fitted; (3) any warranty on the new tap and your fitting work; (4) before and after photos if you have them. Please also tell us whether you found a cause for the cloudy water, such as limescale. The invoice should cover only the kitchen tap job at this address. Thank you.

args.subject: Kitchen tap – can you confirm it is fixed? 18 Thistlewick Row
args.body: Hello Nia, the plumber has invoiced for a new kitchen mixer tap at 18 Thistlewick Row, Fenmere, ZZ1 1ZZ. Could you confirm that the new tap has been fitted and has stopped dripping? Is the water still cloudy when you fill a glass? We are waiting for the invoice details from the plumber. We have noted your loose kitchen drawer with the snapped brackets and will deal with it as a separate request. Please send a photo of it if you can.

args.reason: Waiting for Provider: invoice with an amount (no quote or amount in the case), visit date and completion confirmation. Waiting for Tenant to confirm the tap is fixed.

args.summary: The corrected invoice (event 22 and the attachment) shows no amount, and there was no quote. I asked the contractor for a full invoice and completion details, and asked the tenant to confirm the tap is fixed. A follow-up is set for 2025-09-18.
facts: The landlord approved the plumbing work generally, with no amount stated (events 2-3).
The contractor never gave a quote despite requests (events 4, 5, 8, 11).
The visit was confirmed for 10 September (event 16), but no completion message or visit report is recorded.
The invoice for a new mono kitchen tap was corrected to the right postcode (events 19-22, corrected-plumbing-invoice.pdf). It has a reference and a description but no amount, VAT or date of work.
The tenant's loose-drawer report (event 12) is a separate issue and is unanswered.
The boiler remark in the call (event 21) is not part of this job.
conflicts: The tenant asked about a possible new tap and limescale, but the contractor replaced the tap with no recorded diagnosis or quote.
The invoice postcode was wrong at first and has been corrected.
Event 13 notes confusion over the property address.
missing: Date of attendance and confirmation the work is complete
Tenant confirmation that the drip has stopped and whether the water is still cloudy
Landlord approval of any cost once the amount is known
options_rejected: Forward the invoice to the landlord for payment: there is no amount to forward and no quote to compare it with.
Approve the invoice: it cannot be checked against any quote or approved sum.
Close the case: completion is unconfirmed, and the drawer and cloudy-water issues are open.
Escalate: one message to the contractor can settle what is missing.
args.uncertainty: It is not certain that the tap was fitted on 10 September, because no visit report exists. The cost is unknown, so it may exceed what the landlord expected and need fresh approval.
